consistency_check:
The consistency of the outcome of the modelling phase can be evaluated through several scalar metrics. Here are the results:

* Mean Absolute Error (MAE): The MAE measures the average absolute difference between the predicted and actual values. The current MAE value of 0.2321 is lower than the historical average of 0.2569, indicating improved consistency in the predictions. This means that the model is better at predicting the actual claim frequency compared to previous models.
* R-squared: The R-squared value measures the proportion of the variation in the actual claim frequency that is explained by the model. The current R-squared value of 0.0022 is lower than the historical average of 0.0081, indicating a decrease in the consistency of the predictions. This could be due to the model not capturing all the underlying factors that affect claim frequency.

Based on these metrics, it appears that the model has improved its consistency in predicting claim frequency compared to previous models. However, there is still room for improvement, particularly in capturing the full complexity of the claim frequency. To further improve the consistency of the model, additional analysis and refinement of the model may be necessary.
